title: NBA Offseason Daily Digest
subtitle: July 28, 2026: LeBron James' blockbusters ignite free agency dominoes!

items.headline: LeBron James Signs with Philadelphia 76ers in Blockbuster Free Agency Move
items.summary: The NBA world was rocked as LeBron James officially inked a two-year, $8 million deal with the Philadelphia 76ers. The 41-year-old superstar's decision, announced by the team on Monday, ends weeks of speculation and positions the 76ers as immediate championship contenders, much to the excitement of managing owner Josh Harris.

items.headline: Harden, Green Expected to Re-Sign with Respective Teams Following LeBron's Decision
items.summary: With LeBron James headed to Philadelphia, James Harden is now anticipated to finalize a new multi-year deal with the Cleveland Cavaliers after declining a $42.3 million player option. Similarly, Draymond Green is expected to re-sign with the Golden State Warriors, both resolving their futures this week after their teams pursued James.

items.headline: Denver Nuggets Lock Up Core Pieces with Key Signings
items.summary: The reigning champions, Denver Nuggets, are focused on continuity this offseason. They successfully matched the Oklahoma City Thunder's two-year, $12 million offer sheet for Spencer Jones, retaining the restricted free agent. Additionally, the Nuggets have offered forward Peyton Watson a five-year contract worth $70 million, coming off his best season averaging 14.6 points.

items.headline: Warriors Reportedly Passed on Blockbuster Jaylen Brown Trade
items.summary: In a revealing report, the Golden State Warriors reportedly declined a major opportunity to acquire All-NBA forward Jaylen Brown at last season's trade deadline. The Boston Celtics sought four first-round picks for Brown, a price the Warriors were unwilling to meet, a decision now seen as potentially significant after their pursuit of LeBron James fell short.

items.headline: Stephen Curry Trade Rumors Surface Amidst Warriors' Offseason
items.summary: Unexpected trade rumors surrounding Stephen Curry have emerged this summer, fueled by the Warriors missing out on LeBron James and injuries to key players. While skepticism remains about an actual trade, rival executives are reportedly encouraging Curry to consider other options, with the Charlotte Hornets being mentioned.

items.headline: Veterans Kyle Lowry and Garrett Temple Announce Retirements
items.summary: Two long-time NBA veterans have officially retired this July. Kyle Lowry, an NBA champion with the Toronto Raptors in 2019 and the last active player from the 2006 draft, announced his retirement after 20 seasons on July 7th. Garrett Temple also retired on July 4th, transitioning to an assistant coaching role with the Dallas Mavericks after a 17-year career.

items.headline: Dave Joerger Joins Denver Nuggets Coaching Staff
items.summary: Former Grizzlies and Kings head coach Dave Joerger is returning to the NBA sidelines, joining David Adelman's coaching staff as an assistant for the Denver Nuggets. Joerger turned down an opportunity to coach in the EuroLeague with Paris to remain in the league.
